text:
Invasion of mammalian tissue by fly larvae. Furuncular myiasis may be caused
by Dermatobia hominis or the Tumbu fly Cordylobia anthropophaga. Larvae
of D hominis are often transferred by mosquitoes. The usual host is cattle.
People living near cattle-rearing areas are particularly vulnerable. Eggs, living
larvae, or both are deposited on the skin or mucous membranes or on clothing.
The eggs hatch and produce larvae that then burrow into the skin and cause mild
or severe inflammatory changes.
